problem: Existing goal-oriented VLN/zero-shot navigation methods are tied to specific robot platforms, have high VLM latency, pay little attention to collision safety, and rely on fixed vocabularies or a single goal modality.
motivation: Real deployment needs one system that works across humanoid, quadruped and wheeled robots, runs in real time, avoids obstacles safely, and handles open-vocabulary goals given as category, image or text. The authors split slow semantic reasoning (VLM) from fast local control (DRL) to meet both needs.
key_idea: A cerebrum-cerebellum hierarchy: a single VLM-centred three-layer (semantic/spatial/rule) high-level planner sets goals, and a dimension-configurable DRL local planner executes fast, safe, cross-embodiment control.
insight: A single VLM used for goal parsing, open-vocabulary grounding, semantic waypoint exploration and two-stage verification gives large gains over prior training-free and universal methods, especially on text-goal (39.8 vs 20.2 SR for UniGoal). However, the paper reports no ablations, so which component drives the gains is not isolated. The comparison also leans on a much larger VLM (Qwen3-VL-32B) than earlier baselines, which likely accounts for part of the gain.
method: Cerebellum local planner: SAC-based DRL policy outputting (v, ω) from local observations only (mapless), with goal, current velocity and velocity/acceleration limits as input.

Dimension-aware point encoding: each scan point is encoded as (sinφ, cosφ, 1/(d-β), L_front, L_rear, W/2) and processed by a PointNet (shared MLP + max-pool), so the policy can handle varying robot sizes and sensors.
Curriculum training: robots are grouped by perimeter and moved to progressively harder (shrinking free space) scenarios once group success exceeds 90%, giving zero-shot cross-embodiment transfer.
Semantic layer: the VLM parses the goal (category/text/image) into a profile <core category, attributes, context relations> and produces JSON bounding boxes, which are projected to 3D via depth.
Spatial layer: BEV free/occupied/unknown map; hybrid exploration combining VLM-chosen semantic floor waypoints with frontiers scored by J(f)=I(f)/(D+ε)·M_vis using an FMM geodesic distance.

Rule layer: alternates exploration and confirmation; two-stage VLM verification (global scene check, then cropped instance match) commits a goal only if V=1; adaptive cooldown (long if target absent, short if instance mismatch) limits VLM calls; builds a semantic scene graph.
Real-world system: RGB-only depth estimated with VGGT, plus Livox MID-360 LiDAR for the BEV map and cerebellum obstacle avoidance, on a Unitree Go2 over WLAN.

setting.backbone: Cerebrum: Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct (frozen, via Ollama); Cerebellum: PointNet + SAC DRL policy (trained in simulation)
setting.training_data: Cerebrum: none (training-free). Cerebellum: DRL in simulation with curriculum; data scale not given.
setting.observation: RGB-D 640x480, 79° HFOV in simulation; real world RGB with VGGT-estimated depth plus 3D LiDAR
setting.action_space: Cerebrum outputs 2D goal coordinates on a map; cerebellum outputs continuous velocity (v, ω); simulation uses the built-in Habitat local planner
setting.privileged: none (simulation results use only the Cerebrum with the simulator's built-in planner)

numbers_note: Splits are not stated in the paper; 'val' is an assumption. No quantitative real-world results, no ablations and no cerebellum-specific numbers are given (real-world results are a single qualitative umbrella trial; G1 and wheeled experiments are deferred).
results: FSUNav_Cerebrum beats every listed baseline on all reported tasks: 76.2 SR / 40.49 SPL on HM3D ObjectNav (vs CogNav 72.5/26.2), 48.75/26.93 on MP3D ObjectNav (vs CogNav 46.6/16.1), 72.6/34.88 on IIN (vs IEVE 70.2/25.2), 39.8/21.58 on text-goal (vs UniGoal 20.2/11.4) and 56.87/32.59 on OVON (vs MTU3D 40.8/12.1). The real-world demo is one qualitative open-vocabulary 'umbrella' run on a Go2 at 0.6 m/s.
limitations: No ablations, and the simulation evaluation covers only the Cerebrum; the cerebellum's cross-embodiment and safety claims are not quantitatively verified.
Real-world evidence is a single qualitative demo on a quadruped; humanoid and wheeled experiments are deferred to later versions.
Relies on a large 32B VLM with frequent queries, so latency and the fairness of comparison with smaller-model baselines are unclear (no latency numbers given).
